paper.title: The Single-Copy Quantum Bandit Is Classical: An Exact Spectral Collapse

settings.name_in_paper: States-as-arms quantum bandit with single-copy policies (Pi_1)
unmapped: Arms are unknown quantum states rho_k on a d-dimensional Hilbert space; mean reward mu_k = Tr(rho_k F) for a known effect 0<=F<=I
Each pull gives one fresh copy that the learner measures with an adaptively/randomly chosen finite-outcome POVM; the observation is the measurement outcome
Model class: all quantum states; effective classical outcome laws on the known finite alphabet spec(F)
Assumptions 0<mu_k for all k and mu_star < lambda_max(F); F eigenvalues distinct in spectral decomposition
settings.definition_quote: A single-copy policy ($\pi\in\Pi_1$): at round $t$ it selects an arm $A_t$ and a finite-outcome POVM $M_t$, both measurably (possibly at random) from the record $(A_s,M_s,X_s)_{s<t}$, measures the fresh copy of $\rho_{A_t}$ with $M_t$, and observes the outcome $X_t$.

settings.name_in_paper: States-as-arms quantum bandit with quantum-memory policies (Pi_all) (lower bound)
unmapped: Arms are unknown quantum states; reward mean Tr(rho_k F) for known effect F
Learner may store copies in a quantum register and apply arbitrary record-controlled quantum instruments jointly to all stored copies (collective measurements)
settings.definition_quote: A quantum-memory policy ($\pi\in\Pi_{\mathrm{all}}$) may instead store copies in a quantum register and, in each round, apply an arbitrary record-controlled quantum instrument to the entire register before selecting the next arm

algorithms.name: Spectral-KL-UCB (spectral measurement of F + empirical finite-support KL-UCB)

symbols.Kinf_i: alphabet-restricted Burnetas-Katehakis functional of the spectral statistics of arm i w.r.t. mu_star (equals measured-relative-entropy distance to confusing half-space)

conditions: holds for adaptive and randomized measurement choice

source.label: thm:lbsc
source.quote: For every consistent $\pi\in\Pi_1$ and every suboptimal arm $k$, \liminf_{T\to\infty} \frac{\mathbb E[N_k(T)]}{\ln T} \ge \frac{1}{\Minf(k)} = \frac{1}{\Kinf(k)}.

results.notes: Bound on expected pull count of arm k. Remark 3 extends it to delayed single-copy measurement policies.

symbols.Kinf_i: alphabet-restricted Burnetas-Katehakis functional of arm i's spectral statistics

tuning: threshold l(t,n)=ln t + 3 ln ln t + (L-1)/2 ln n + c_L

source.label: thm:match
source.quote: Let \textsc{Spectral-KL-UCB} measure every pulled copy with the spectral POVM $\{P_i\}$ of $F$ and play the index policy of Section~\ref{sec:finite}. Then for every suboptimal $k$, $\limsup_T\mathbb E[N_k(T)]/\ln T\le1/\Kinf(k)$; combined with Theorem~\ref{thm:lbsc}, \lim R(T)/\ln T = \sum_{k\ne k^\star}\Delta_k/\Kinf(k)

results.notes: Pull-count statement limsup E[N_k]/ln T <= 1/Kinf(k); for projector F, Kinf reduces to kl(mu_k, mu_star). Corollary 2 proves it from Theorem 4.

symbols.Kinf_i: alphabet-restricted Burnetas-Katehakis functional of arm i's spectral statistics

source.label: thm:match
source.quote: No consistent single-copy strategy --- adaptive, randomized, tomographic, or otherwise --- improves the leading constant over measuring the reward observable itself.

results.notes: Regret-level lower bound obtained by combining Theorem 2 with the regret decomposition, as stated in Theorem 3.

symbols.n_delta: smallest integer n >= max{1, ceil(a/b_k)} with n*b_k >= ln T + 3 ln ln T + (L-1)/2 ln n + c_L, where a=(L-1)/2, b_k=Kinf(k)-delta_an
symbols.L: number of distinct eigenvalues of F (alphabet size)
symbols.eps_k: delta_an/G_k, G_k = max_i |ln(1 - lambda*(f_i - mu_star))| subgradient constant from Lemma 2

tuning: threshold l(t,n)=ln t + 3 ln ln t + (L-1)/2 ln n + c_L

source.label: thm:finite
source.quote: Under the model of Section~\ref{sec:model}, for every integer $T\ge3$, every suboptimal arm $k$ and every $\delta\in(0,\Kinf(q_k))$, with $G_k$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:dual} and $\varepsilon_k:=\delta/G_k$: \mathbb E[N_k(T)] \le n_\delta(T) + \frac{2^L-2}{e^{\varepsilon_k^2/2}-1} + 3.

results.notes: Bound on expected pull count; the algorithm's index is anytime but the bound is stated for each T, recorded as known/each T. Paper's delta is an analysis parameter, not a confidence level.

symbols.Dinf_i: inf over states sigma with Tr(sigma F) >= mu_star of the Umegaki relative entropy D(rho_i || sigma)

source.label: thm:univ
source.quote: For every consistent $\pi\in\Pi_{\mathrm{all}}$ and suboptimal $k$, \liminf_{T\to\infty} \frac{\mathbb E[N_k(T)]}{\ln T} \ge \frac{1}{\Dinf(k)}, and consequently $\liminf_T R(T)/\ln T\ge\sum_{k\ne k^\star}\Delta_k/\Dinf(k)$.

results.notes: Also per-arm pull-count bound (r6). Dinf = Kinf iff arm commutes with F (Corollary 4).

symbols.Dinf_i: inf over states sigma with Tr(sigma F) >= mu_star of the Umegaki relative entropy D(rho_i || sigma)

source.label: thm:univ
source.quote: For every consistent $\pi\in\Pi_{\mathrm{all}}$ and suboptimal $k$, \liminf_{T\to\infty} \frac{\mathbb E[N_k(T)]}{\ln T} \ge \frac{1}{\Dinf(k)}
